prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: production pixel-art character DESIGN REFERENCE sheet for an advanced SWORDMASTER in a tactical RPG, promotion of a simple swordsman. Four full-body views in a 2x2 grid: upper-left FRONT, upper-right LEFT SIDE PROFILE, lower-left BACK, lower-right BATTLE three-quarter view facing LEFT resting ONE long straight sword diagonally on right shoulder (blade extends up-right behind head). Same man and same outfit in all four views. Make him visibly stronger than an ordinary short-tunic swordsman through broader ivory armored shoulder guards, fitted blue layered short tunic, ivory V collar and solid ivory edging, robust blue/navy greaves and gauntlets, and a short one-sided BLUE CLOTH CAPE attached behind shoulders, ending around hip/knee. The cape is SOFT CLOTH, not a shield. No shield anywhere. Clearly readable normal peach skin face and eyes, simple pure dark navy hair without highlights, confident young adult. Restrained soft gold belt clasp and shoulder fasteners, not ornate decorations. EXACT six colors only: dark navy #172638 (hair, outline and deepest shadow), blue #3976B5, ivory #E4E1C8, peach skin #DDA77D, dark blue #2C527E (one necessary fold/shadow tone), muted gold #B5A16C (small accent). Keep bright blue/ivory areas clean and contiguous, matte, not grey or washed-out. Chunky SNES tactical map pixel art, crisp squares, no gradients, no texture, no glossy highlights, no dithering, no scattered white speckles. Armor still lightweight enough for jumping sword attacks. No text, labels, pedestal, shadows, background effects, magic, extra weapons or props. Genuine transparent background. Consistent scale, well separated views, every sword/cape/foot complete with generous empty margins.
